doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
title: The Herman saxophone section and Woody's tax troubles
summary: The Italian sax section and Woody dodging the IRS out the back door.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well the saxophone section was strictly Italian. It was Sal Nestico and Joe Romano and Carmen Leggio.

Oh it was wonderful. It was really wonderful. And it was a good band. And Woody was going through some bad times because things were rough on the road and Woody was having to deal with income tax problems and some nights he would just say, “I’ll see you all later” and he would dodge out the back because he had this thing about spotting people. He could spot an IRS man coming in the door, and he’d be out the back door and gone.
But Woody was a great experience.
